title: Bounds for the halting-number approximation
statement: For every finite Boolean string $x$, let $N$ be the length of the output of the head transducer on $x$, and let $J$ be the base-$4$ logarithm, rounded down, of the length of the output of the rest transducer on $x$. If $x$ belongs to the language of strings satisfying $J \ge 1$, $N$ equal to the halting-bit prefix through position $J-1$, and a halting bit at position $J-1$, then $4N+1 \le H4^J \le 4N+4/3$, where $H$ is the halting coin. If $x$ does not belong to that language, then $H4^J \le 4N+1/3$ or $4N+4 \le H4^J$.
hypotheses_covered: Either $x$ belongs to the specified halting language or it does not.
